Definition: assumed by some as the base of certain irregular forms of G1492; to know:--know.
BiblicalUsage: To know is what the old scholars guessed this word meant, but the word itself never appears in the Greek New Testament as it stands. It was assumed to be the base of certain forms of the verb to know, yet no verse in the Greek text carries this form, so no passage can be cited for it.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the honest thing is to say so plainly: a word that never occurs cannot teach me anything, and I will not invent a verse for it.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
